title: Extreme value theory to estimate the probability of rare catastrophic outputs without observing them

original_idea.body:
# Extreme value theory to estimate the probability of rare catastrophic outputs without observing them

**Problem:** Open Phil flags estimating the probability of rare misbehavior as a starred problem. Standard sampling can't estimate the frequency of catastrophic outputs that occur far out in the tail and are essentially never seen in normal sampling.

**Direction:** Borrow Extreme Value Theory (EVT) and peaks-over-threshold modeling from hydrology/finance. Score many sampled outputs of a small open model on a continuous harm/toxicity scale, fit a Generalized Pareto Distribution to the tail above a high threshold, and extrapolate the probability of exceeding a catastrophic-harm level. Validate the extrapolation by holding out the most extreme samples and checking the GPD's predictive coverage.

**Why it matters:** Provides a principled white-box-free estimate of rare-event risk from feasible sample sizes — directly targeting a starred open problem with a method labs rarely apply. Pure inference + statistics on consumer hardware.

**Relevant context:** EVT/GPD are standard in risk modeling (Coles, Embrechts). Landscape honesty_faithfulness open problem: 'estimate probability of rare misbehavior without observing it'. Source subfield: extreme value theory / risk modeling. Target subfield: evaluations_benchmarks, honesty_faithfulness.
